title: Rerank per-vector volume + committed-tier pricing pilot and QSA artifact pack
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a controlled pilot that introduces a per-vector pricing lane for reranking requests with two committed tiers and automated batch-discounting logic. The goal is to validate price sensitivity, enterprise legal/QSA requirements alignment, and unit economics at three scale bands for customers who use large bulk rerank jobs or embeddings-heavy reranking flows. Product work includes pricing spec, billing contract language, API surface notes, and a QSA artifact pack for enterprise procurement teams.
background: Enterprise customers and renewals teams repeatedly ask for: (1) per-vector clarity on rerank/embedding unit costs, (2) predictable committed-tier discounts for high-volume customers, and (3) defensible security artifacts (QSA) that can be attached to contract negotiations. Current hosted pricing is per-embedding-call and lacks explicit batch-discount mechanics for rerank flows that send thousands of vectors in a single job. Without a pilot, sales are resorting to ad-hoc discounts; we need a repeatable product + contract construct.
proposal: Introduce: (A) a 3-tier committed volume pricing model for rerank vectors (Bronze/1M, Silver/10M, Gold/100M monthly committed vectors) with stepped per-vector rates; (B) an automated batch-discount algorithm that applies a supplemental discount based on observed median batch size and tail latency; (C) standardized contract language and an asset pack for QSA responses (data flow diagrams, KMS integration details, retention policies). Pilot will be offered to 4 customers in the sales pipeline and 2 internal DA test accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Pricing spec document reviewed and approved by Legal and RevOps
Billing prototype generates correct invoice line items for committed tiers and batch discounts in the staging billing sandbox
QSA artifact pack compiled: network diagram, encryption-at-rest checklist, SOC2 reference, retention policy, sample SLA clause
Two sales pilots signed with commitments and one internal pilot validates cost math
Telemetry dashboard shows per-vector revenue, average batch size, and cost per vector across pilot customers
experiment_design: A/B style pilot where consenting enterprise customers are offered the new committed per-vector tier vs. the existing blended per-call pricing. Track: conversion rate on proposal, change in monthly committed vectors, effective per-vector price, churn risk signals, and quality regressions (if any) tied to quantization/variant substitution. Run for 90 days per pilot customer with weekly telemetry reviews. Use synthetic workloads to simulate 10x/100x scale to model unit economics before full rollout.
qsa_checklist: Complete RFQ/Questionnaire template for procurement (answers + references)
Provide KMS/HSM integration notes and key rotation policy
Attach SOC2 Type II report or SOC2 summary page
Network diagram showing private link/VPC options and data flow for rerank jobs
Documented data retention and deletion workflow for cached embeddings
List of third-party subprocessors and subprocessors' security posture summary
dependencies: ENG-4590 (api: batch size hint + metadata header for rerank calls)
PM-20523 (prior embed batch credit experiment - learnings)
milestones: 2026-01-20: Pilot review and go/no-go for 2026 rollout
notes: Trade-offs discussed: simpler flat slab vs. stepped tier with batch modifier — stepped tier + modifier preferred to avoid sudden cliffs for customers.
Consider adding a minimum commitment credit to guard margin in low-usage months.
Need to confirm whether Private (VPC) customers require separate contract language for batch data caching.
Potential ops risk: billing retroactive adjustments for prior month usage; finance wants a manual approval workflow for credits.
